long_biography.plain_text:
Fresh from law school, Segal moved from New York to a depressed Texas property market and bought an empty office block for a fraction of its construction cost. Banks would not finance the deposit, so his mother committed her savings and friends supplied additional equity. Low acquisition costs let him offer inexpensive, flexible space, and the first building filled within a year.

He repeated that formula across older suburban offices: acquire cheaply, improve operations, publish straightforward rents and accept smaller tenants on shorter leases. Boxer later added retail centres, hotels, coworking suites and property-management services, but offices remain the foundation of the national portfolio. Segal continues to direct acquisitions and strategy as chairman and chief executive.
